items.title: Four million employee records, 2.5 million medical files and 6,000 users make the platform the system of record for large employers' occupational health
items.summary: Kitry states more than 35 years of expertise, 4M+ employee records followed, 6,000+ active users and named references including SNCF, Thales, Ville de Paris, Ville de Bruxelles, Umicore, Engie, BNP, EIB, Stellantis, EDF, RATP, CNRS, Disney and BASF. Vortex's investment page reports that 150+ organisations rely on Kitry and that more than 2.5 million medical files are stored via the platform, across healthcare, chemicals, financial services, manufacturing and government in Belgium, France and the Netherlands.
items.implication: The unit of value is the employer's complete, historical health-and-safety record, not a feature: protect data continuity (migration without loss, 40-year retention, transfer between services) and price on workforce size and modules, because a customer that has moved decades of medical files onto the platform will not switch on a feature comparison.

items.title: More than half of employees at Kitry's French, Belgian and Luxembourg customers already use self-service, so the portal carries the consultation day
items.summary: Kitry reports that 50%+ of employees at its FR/BE/LU customers use the self-service portals. The occupational health module offers a web calendar with online booking and automated SMS reminders, interactive web questionnaires that prepare the visit, secure teleconsultation with real-time document sharing and integrated signature, automated import of results from connected measurement devices, and a separate Employee and Manager Portals module.
items.implication: Treat self-service rate as a north-star metric per customer rather than a nice-to-have: every appointment an employee books, moves or prepares online removes nurse administration, reduces no-shows and makes the physician's slot productive, while the manager portal must show fitness status and restrictions without ever exposing medical content.

items.title: France's 2021 prevention law and the 2022 DMST decree fix the medical file's content, access rules, 40-year retention and inter-service transfer, and mandate interoperable occupational health systems
items.summary: Law 2021-1018 of 2 August 2021 strengthens prevention in occupational health: it defines the dossier médical en santé au travail (DMST), introduces the prevention passport in which the employer records training attestations, and requires that information systems used by occupational health professionals conform to interoperability standards, with the relevant provisions entering into force no later than 1 January 2024. Decree 2022-1434 of 15 November 2022 specifies the DMST content (identity, current and past exposures, health information from visits, opinions and recommendations), access and delegation rules with every action traced and time-stamped, the worker's right to oppose access and sharing, retention for forty years from the last visit, hosting with approved organisations, transfer between services, and compliance of existing files by 31 March 2023.
items.implication: The medical file brick and its confidentiality model are regulated artefacts: implement the DMST structure, role-based access with full audit trail, worker opposition and consent, interoperability standards and inter-service transfer as product features maintained by the regulatory content team, and use each legal change as a release event that keeps customers current rather than a per-customer project.

items.title: HDS certification, ISO 27001 and EEA-only access are the entry ticket for hosting occupational medical data in France, and Kitry sells hosting as a product tier
items.summary: The Agence du Numérique en Santé describes HDS (Hébergeur de données de santé) certification as an assessment of health-data hosting providers against a certification referential, with certificates issued for three years and annual surveillance audits, and with recognition of existing ISO 27001 certifications during the compliance audit. Kitry states it is HDS and ISO 27001 certified, offers Shared SaaS and Dedicated SaaS hosting, guarantees no data access from non-EEA countries and no risk of access imposed by third-country legislation, and names Cegedim.cloud as its hosting subcontractor and Goodflag for electronic signature.
items.implication: Certification and residency are the security review that decides a tender, so keep HDS, ISO 27001 and EEA-only hosting as a productised tier (shared or dedicated) with evidence packs ready for the coordinator's procurement and DPO, and make the hosting subcontractor chain part of the contract rather than a surprise in due diligence.

items.title: French surveillance periodicity is a rule table — three months, five years, four years, two years — that the platform must compute per worker and exposure
items.summary: The French Labour Code requires a visite d'information et de prévention within three months of taking up the post (R4624-10), renewed at intervals not exceeding five years (R4624-16). Workers on posts with particular risks — exposure to asbestos, lead, carcinogenic or mutagenic agents, biological agents of groups 3 and 4, ionising radiation, hyperbaric conditions, work at height on scaffolding, and any post requiring a specific aptitude examination — receive enhanced individual monitoring (R4624-23) with an aptitude examination renewed at most every four years and an intermediate visit by a health professional no later than two years after (R4624-28).
items.implication: Surveillance rules must be a configurable engine keyed on country, exposure profile and workstation, fed by HRIS assignments, so that a change of post recalculates the next due examination automatically; compliance rate per category is the KPI the service manager reports and the physician is judged on.

items.title: The DUERP is mandatory from the first employee, updated yearly, kept forty years in successive versions and transmitted to the occupational health service
items.summary: According to INRS, the document unique d'évaluation des risques professionnels is mandatory for every enterprise from the hiring of the first employee, must be updated at least annually in companies with 11 or more employees and whenever a significant change or new risk information arises, must be preserved in its successive versions for at least forty years, and each updated version must be transmitted to the occupational health service. Enterprises with 50 or more employees must derive an annual prevention programme (PAPRIPACT) with measures, timelines, cost estimates and owners; smaller ones document prevention actions in the DUERP itself. The dematerialised deposit portal foreseen by law is, per INRS, still not available.
items.implication: Version every risk assessment with date, author and workstation scope, generate the action plan from it, and expose the current version to the physician automatically; the forty-year archive and the transmission obligation make the safety module and the medical file one connected record, which is Kitry's differentiator against standalone EHS tools.

items.title: Belgium requires an internal prevention service in every company and an external service where the internal one cannot deliver, which is where IDEWE and Mensura dominate
items.summary: Under the Belgian Act of 4 August 1996 and the Code on well-being at work, every employer must set up an internal service for prevention and protection at work with one or more prevention advisers, group companies A to D by risk and size, draw up a global prevention plan and an annual action plan, and constitute a Committee for Prevention and Protection at Work above 50 employees; where the internal service cannot execute all tasks — in particular health surveillance — the employer must use an accredited external service, a non-profit with ISO 9001 certification, organised in a risk management section and a health supervision section led by an occupational physician. IDEWE describes itself as Belgium's largest external service, supporting 35,000 employers and nearly 880,000 employees with more than 1,000 experts; Mensura reports a team of over 800 specialists.
items.implication: Kitry's Belgian buyer is the large organisation whose internal service runs its own health surveillance; the external services are both substitutes and integration partners, so model the global prevention plan, annual action plan and committee reporting as first-class features and offer file transfer and reporting interfaces to external services rather than competing for their SME base.

items.title: Belgian occupational disease declarations run through Fedris on prescribed forms, with the physician's certificate mandatory and the employer's exposure attestation optional
items.summary: Fedris, the Belgian federal agency for occupational risks, handles occupational disease compensation for private-sector workers (forms 501 claim and 503 medical certificate) and for provincial and local administrations (forms 601 and 603), accepting electronic or paper submissions with electronic filing enabling smoother case processing; supporting medical documents are mandatory while employer attestations proving workplace exposure are welcome but not obligatory, and public-sector claims pass through the employer's designated department. EU-OSHA's country profile notes that Fedris also controls private accident insurers and promotes prevention.
items.implication: National forms and connectors are country content: keep Fedris and insurer forms, French CERFA and Ameli declarations pre-filled from the worker, workstation and exposure record so HR declares on time with the right evidence, and let the physician's certificate and the exposure history come from the same file that the DUERP and the chemical inventory feed.

items.title: 2.83 million non-fatal and 3,298 fatal accidents at work in the EU in 2023 keep accident declaration and analysis a board-level obligation
items.summary: Eurostat's ESAW data for 2023 record 2.83 million non-fatal accidents at work (down 5% from 2.98 million in 2022) and 3,298 fatal accidents (12 more than in 2022), giving incidence rates of 1,393 non-fatal and 1.63 fatal accidents per 100,000 employed people, with the fatal rate below 2 per 100,000 since 2016. Manufacturing accounted for 18.5% of non-fatal accidents, construction 12.9%, distributive trades 12.2% and health and social work 12.1%; 67.6% of non-fatal accidents involved men; construction held 24.0% of fatal accidents, transportation and storage 16.4% and manufacturing 13.4%.
items.implication: Frequency and severity rates per site, normalised per 100,000 hours or employees and benchmarked against sector rates, are what the HSE manager and the works council look at, so accident events must carry sector, site, workstation and cause codes at declaration time and flow into dashboards without re-keying.

items.title: About 2.7 million French private-sector employees report exposure to at least one carcinogenic chemical, so chemical inventory, exposure groups and enhanced surveillance must share one record
items.summary: INRS cites the SUMER 2017 survey: about 11% of France's active population, 2.7 million private-sector employees, report exposure at work to at least one carcinogenic chemical agent. The employer must inventory products and work situations that may expose workers to CMR agents, remove or substitute them whenever technically possible, and track and control remaining exposure. Kitry's safety module includes a centralised chemical product inventory with safety data sheets and chemical risk evaluation, management of homogeneous exposure groups (GHE) and workstations with their risks and PPE, and measurement campaigns for noise, dust, vibrations and air quality.
items.implication: Link every chemical product and measurement campaign to workstations and exposure groups so that CMR exposure automatically places workers under enhanced surveillance, populates the exposure history in the medical file and survives forty years for later occupational disease claims; this traceability chain is what an inspector and a Fedris or Ameli case will ask for.

items.title: French rivals are funded and broad — Padoa raised EUR 80 million and Val Solutions covers 12 million employees — so Kitry competes on internal services, configuration and AI-assisted consultations
items.summary: On 2 February 2022 the French start-up padoa announced an EUR 80 million round led by Five Arrows Growth Capital (Rothschild & Co) alongside majority shareholder Kamet Ventures, to expand its software and hire 60 people in 2022. Val Solutions states that its uEgar platform follows 12 million employees, serves 600 occupational health services (inter-company, in-company and public sector) and 12,000 health professionals, with HDS and ISO 27001 hosting, HL7 interoperability and integrated AI. Kitry positions its occupational health module for internal services with customisable visit protocols, complete access traceability, automatic HR synchronisation, automatic generation of mandatory procedures and Europe-based AI for summarising consultations.
items.implication: Do not chase the French inter-company SPSTI market where Val Solutions and Padoa concentrate; win the internal services of large employers and public bodies across FR/BE/LU/NL on configurability, migration of legacy files and certified hosting, and treat consultation summarisation and assisted drafting as the next differentiator, under physician supervision and inside the HDS perimeter.

items.title: Vortex's 2022 buyout funds the 'Kitry as a Service' transition and international rollout on top of a four-phase implementation and support model
items.summary: On 29 March 2022 Kitry Group, based in Antwerp, announced a strategic partnership with Vortex Capital Partners to accelerate commercial expansion, further international rollout and intensified product development around the 'Kitry as a Service' offering; the release cites more than 100 customers including blue-chip companies and public-sector organisations in Belgium, France and the Netherlands, Kitry's support for achieving and maintaining ISO 45001, and Vortex's view of a 'triple-A client base'. Kitry's delivery model comprises functional study, configuration, project management and role-specific training, followed by change management, data migration from external systems without loss, reactive support and a dedicated account manager for each client, in French, English and Dutch.
items.implication: Growth beyond the founder-led base depends on repeatable implementations: standardise the four phases and the migration toolkit so consultants take customers live on schedule, keep every tenant on the release train, and use ISO 45001-ready safety features and Dutch-language regulatory content to open the Netherlands and new sectors without bespoke projects.
